districts.status: Incumbent retiring to run for Senate

backtests.note: Each election forecast from the other elections at each distance from election day; seats are the Democrats'.

2026.note: 2026 forecast from the elections before it (2018-2024), none of it fitted on 2026; scored on the winners as Wikipedia gave them on the day read

tested.idea: Each district at the national vote plus its lean, nothing fitted
tested.result: A typical contested race missed by 3.7 points, 2012-2024, even with the national vote known

tested.idea: A member of either party on the November ballot
tested.result: A typical miss of 3.2 points and 60 more races called, 2012-2024

tested.idea: Fitted on 2018 onward rather than 2012 onward
tested.result: A member was worth about 4 to 7 points to their party in 2012-2016 and about 2 to 3 since 2018: the House has become national, so the older years would overstate it

tested.idea: Leans for 2018 and 2020 worked out the way Cook has since 2022 (three parts the last presidential election, one part the one before)
tested.result: Brier score 0.032 against 0.035 with the even split Cook published then, and eight more races called; it is the lean the live forecast reads

tested.idea: The district's last House result on the same lines
tested.result: Added nothing once the lean and the member were in (a typical miss of 3.3 points against 3.2)

tested.idea: A member running on lines new to them counting for less
tested.result: A typical miss of 3.4 points against 3.2

tested.idea: Money raised over the whole cycle
tested.result: A little help in close races, but a forecast cannot know the totals in advance, and the typical miss was 3.3 points against 3.2

tested.idea: Money as it stood on each day (every FEC report of both parties' candidates, 2012-2024, about 70,000)
tested.result: The forecasts of 2018-2024 barely moved: the seat count's typical miss fell by half a seat at some distances and not at others, and the races called and the chances stayed the same
